signals.entity: All EU Member States (AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI in footprint)
signals.signal: Article 5a(1) of Reg (EU) No 910/2014 as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/1183 requires each Member State to provide at least one EU Digital Identity (EUDI) Wallet - a state-provided or state-recognised mobile app holding a citizen's legally valid identity data - 'within 24 months of the date of entry into force of the implementing acts referred to in paragraph 23 of this Article and in Article 5c(6)'. Those first implementing acts (CIR (EU) 2024/2977, 2024/2979, 2024/2980, 2024/2981, 2024/2982) were adopted 28/11/2024, published in the OJ 04/12/2024, and CIR 2024/2977 Art. 6 states it enters into force 'on the twentieth day following that of its publication' = 24/12/2024. The hard national wallet deadline is therefore 24/12/2026.
signals.source_name: EUR-Lex, consolidated Reg (EU) No 910/2014 (CELEX 02014R0910-20241018), Art. 5a(1); CIR (EU) 2024/2977 Art. 6
signals.implies: (a) Affects every state identity issuer in the 10 EU footprint markets and, downstream, every bank that will consume wallet-issued PID (person identification data). (b) Banks need wallet-verifier middleware inside onboarding and login: Printec digital onboarding/eKYC (Namirial) is the direct fit, with Thales HSM/PCI for the keys that sign relying-party requests. (c) Budget must commit now - the deadline is under 5 months away and the bank-side acceptance obligation lands exactly 12 months later.
signals.likelihood: Certain as a legal deadline; national delivery slippage likely in several markets
signals.followup: Track each footprint MS's notified wallet solution via the Commission ecosystem notification channel (CIR 2024/2980) after 24/12/2026.

signals.entity: Banks, PSPs and e-money institutions in all EU footprint markets (AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, GR, HU, RO, SK, SI)
signals.signal: Article 5f(2) of the consolidated eIDAS Regulation: private relying parties (excluding micro and small enterprises per Recommendation 2003/361/EC) that are required by Union or national law to use strong user authentication for online identification, or where it is required by contractual obligation - the text explicitly names 'banking, financial services' - 'shall, no later than 36 months from the date of entry into force of the implementing acts referred to in Article 5a(23) and Article 5c(6) and only upon the voluntary request of the user, also accept European Digital Identity Wallets'. With those acts in force from 24/12/2024, the bank acceptance date is 24/12/2027. Article 5f(1) already obliges public sector bodies to accept wallets.
signals.source_name: EUR-Lex, consolidated Reg (EU) No 910/2014 (CELEX 02014R0910-20241018), Art. 5f(1)-(2)
signals.implies: (a) Every medium/large bank in the 10 EU footprint markets: Alpha Bank, Eurobank, NBG, Piraeus (GR); BCR, BRD, Banca Transilvania (RO); OTP, K&H, Erste (HU); UniCredit Bulbank, DSK, Postbank (BG); Zagrebacka, PBZ, Erste (HR); Bank of Cyprus, Hellenic (CY); Erste, RBI, BAWAG (AT); CSOB, KB (CZ); SLSP, VUB (SK); NLB (SI). (b) They must buy a wallet-verifier/relying-party stack inside digital onboarding and login (Printec + Namirial eKYC), relying-party access certificates and HSM key custody behind them (Thales HSM, remote key injection), and changes to customer-identity and card-issuing records. (c) Budget commits 6-12 months ahead: Q4-2026 to mid-2027 planning; RFPs realistically H1-2027.
signals.likelihood: High - statutory, no derogation for banks above SME size
signals.followup: All footprint significant institutions fall outside the micro/small carve-out. Pre-position Namirial wallet-verifier capability in 2027 budget cycles.

signals.entity: Wallet-relying parties (incl. banks) and national relying-party registrars
signals.signal: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/848 of 06/05/2025 sets the rules for registration of wallet-relying parties in national registers and APPLIES FROM 24/12/2026. It was amended by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1730 of 15/07/2026 (OJ 22/07/2026, in force the 20th day after = 11/08/2026), which requires registrars to issue relying-party access certificates 'in an automated manner and without undue delay after the registration', replaces the certificate-policy standard ETSI EN 319 411-1 v1.4.1 (2023-10) with ETSI TS 119 411-8 V1.1.1 (2025-10), and adds a Union-harmonised 'general access policy' field in the certificate telling users which data the relying party may lawfully request.
signals.source_name: EUR-Lex, CIR (EU) 2026/1730 amending CIR (EU) 2025/848
signals.implies: (a) Every footprint bank wanting to read wallet attributes must first be registered in its national wallet-relying-party register and hold a relying-party access certificate under the new ETSI TS 119 411-8 policy. (b) Concrete buy: PKI/certificate lifecycle and key custody (Thales HSM, remote key injection) plus integration work in the identity layer to declare and enforce a data-minimised access policy - a natural attach to Printec eKYC (Namirial) and card/identity management. (c) Registers open 24/12/2026, so the registration+certificate project must be funded in the current 2026 budget round.
signals.likelihood: High
signals.followup: Identify the designated national registrar in each footprint MS (typically the eIDAS supervisory body or ministry of digital governance) once notified to the Commission.

signals.entity: Wallet providers and remote identity-proofing / eKYC vendors serving EU footprint banks
signals.signal: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/798 of 07/04/2026 (OJ 08/04/2026) lays down the reference standards for REMOTE ONBOARDING of users to EUDI Wallets under Art. 5a(24) - permitting enrolment with an eID at assurance level SUBSTANTIAL plus additional procedures that together meet level HIGH. It binds specified clauses of ETSI TS 119 461 V2.1.1 (2025-02) covering attended and unattended remote identity proofing with identity documents, identity proofing via eID authentication, the Baseline-to-Extended Level of Identity Proofing (LoIP) enhancement, and face-biometric validation against the document chip over NFC with chip authentication; ETSI EN 319 401 governs the operational risk assessment and evidence collection.
signals.source_name: EUR-Lex, CIR (EU) 2026/798
signals.implies: (a) Relevant to every footprint bank running remote account opening and to the trust service providers behind national wallets. (b) It fixes the technical bar for remote eKYC: NFC chip read with chip authentication plus a face-biometric match, i.e. a document-chip-capable mobile SDK and a certified identity-proofing back end - exactly the Printec/Namirial digital-onboarding proposition, with Thales HSM behind the signing. Banks running video-only KYC must upgrade. (c) In force already; alignment to ETSI TS 119 461 V2.1.1 must be budgeted in the 2026-2027 cycle to be ready before the 24/12/2027 acceptance date.
signals.likelihood: High
signals.followup: Confirm Namirial's ETSI TS 119 461 V2.1.1 conformity attestation and use it as the compliance shortcut in footprint RFPs.

signals.entity: EUDI Wallet solution providers and bank-side verifier integrators
signals.signal: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1731 of 15/07/2026 (OJ 22/07/2026, in force 11/08/2026) amends the four core wallet implementing acts - CIR (EU) 2024/2977 (person identification data and electronic attestations of attributes), 2024/2979 (wallet integrity and core functionalities), 2024/2980 (ecosystem notifications) and 2024/2982 (protocols and interfaces) - to update applicable standards: ENISA-aligned cryptographic mechanisms, JWT-format wallet unit attestations (wallet instance + key attestations), portrait protection with selective disclosure, the EU Digital Identity Wallet Trust Mark, SD-JWT VC and ISO/IEC mdoc encodings for person identification data, Token Status Lists for revocation, and gatekeeper interoperability via CTAP 2.3.
signals.source_name: EUR-Lex, CIR (EU) 2026/1731
signals.implies: (a) Hits national wallet programmes in all 10 EU footprint markets barely four months before their 24/12/2026 go-live, and any bank building a verifier. (b) Verifier-side impact for Printec: SD-JWT VC and ISO mdoc parsing, Token Status List revocation checking and CTAP 2.3 support must be in the eKYC/authentication stack; the crypto changes touch HSM key profiles (Thales). (c) A standards change this late is a re-work trigger - integration budget needs to move in Q3-Q4 2026.
signals.likelihood: High
signals.followup: Diff the amended annexes against the 2024 baseline to size verifier re-work for Namirial/Printec integrations.

signals.entity: Ministry of Digital Governance & AI / GRNET - gov.gr Wallet
signals.signal: [LOCAL-LANGUAGE SOURCE] Greek Ministry of Digital Governance press release 13/07/2026: the Greek passport becomes the 13th document available in the new version of gov.gr Wallet, usable for identification and as a travel document within Greece (service and diplomatic passports excluded). The release also gives the installed base: over 2.516 million digital police ID cards and over 1.984 million digital driving licences issued into the wallet. Greek title: «Tο ελληνικό διαβατήριο εντάσσεται στα έγγραφα του Gov.gr wallet» [The Greek passport joins the documents in gov.gr Wallet]. The release itself does NOT mention EUDI Wallet or eIDAS 2 - Greece's formal EUDI conversion of gov.gr Wallet is announced only in ministerial statements and press, not in this primary text.
signals.source_name: Υπουργείο Ψηφιακής Διακυβέρνησης (Greek Ministry of Digital Governance), mindigital.gr
signals.implies: (a) Greek banks (Alpha, Eurobank, NBG, Piraeus, Attica, Optima) face a population of ~2.5m citizens already carrying a state digital ID that will become an EUDI Wallet by 24/12/2026. (b) The buy is a gov.gr-Wallet/EUDI verifier in branch and remote onboarding, and in self-service: a wallet-read capability on bank kiosks and ATMs (Printec self-service & bank kiosks, NCR x-core) is a differentiator for identity-verified transactions at the machine, alongside Namirial eKYC for remote channels. (c) With ~2.5m wallets already in field, Greek banks can move ahead of the 2027 obligation - budget conversations belong in the FY2027 plan being written now.
signals.likelihood: High that gov.gr Wallet is Greece's notified EUDI wallet
signals.followup: Obtain the Greek transposition/implementation act designating gov.gr Wallet as the notified EUDI Wallet and the national relying-party registrar (likely MinDigital/GRNET); confirm the Greece-Cyprus wallet interconnection announcement date from a primary ministry release.

signals.entity: Ministry of Internal Affairs (MAI) / DGEP - RoEUDIW 'RO Wallet'
signals.signal: [LOCAL-LANGUAGE SOURCE] Romanian Directorate for Persons Records and Databases Management (DGEP, Ministry of Internal Affairs) statement published 28/01/2026 on the European digital identity wallet project: Romania participates in the EUDIW-PACT project coordinated by the French Ministry of the Interior, bringing together 24 EU Member States and technical partners, built to the common specifications of Reg (EU) 2024/1183. December 2026 is confirmed as the EU-wide deadline for at least one certified EUDI Wallet. DGEP states the electronic identity card (cartea electronica de identitate, CEI) 'will permit enrolment (account creation) in this application and subsequently user authentication for access'. Romanian press (ZF, Economica.net, Digital Skills Romania) additionally reports the government will adopt the German-developed wallet solution rather than build its own, with ADR excluded from the project, and a Senate-adopted bill (March 2026) mandating ROeID or an accredited eID on public-authority platforms within 12 months of entry into force - these commercial/legislative details are PRESS-tier and unconfirmed in a primary text.
signals.source_name: DGEP, Ministerul Afacerilor Interne (Romania) - „Precizare referitoare la ... proiectul portofelului european de identitate digitala si inrolarea/autentificarea cu cartea electronica de identitate"
signals.implies: (a) BCR, BRD, Banca Transilvania, Raiffeisen RO, ING RO, UniCredit RO plus the CEC/Exim state banks. (b) Because Romanian enrolment is anchored on the CEI chip, the bank-side read path is NFC document reading + chip authentication - which is exactly the CIR 2026/798 / ETSI TS 119 461 stack: Printec/Namirial eKYC with NFC SDK, and Thales HSM for relying-party certificates. CEI rollout also makes chip-reading branch/kiosk hardware relevant (Printec self-service kiosks). (c) Romania is a 'project announced' laggard on the EU rollout tracker; a compressed national build means bank integration work slips to 2027 - budget conversations Q4-2026.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that Romania ships a wallet by 24/12/2026; high that it slips into 2027
signals.followup: Find the Romanian normative act (HG/OUG in Monitorul Oficial) formally designating the RoEUDIW operator and the national relying-party registrar; verify the German-solution adoption claim against an ADR/MCID primary release.

signals.entity: Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) supervised institutions - Hungarian banks
signals.signal: [LOCAL-LANGUAGE SOURCE][STANDING - dated 2024/2025, relevant as the pre-EUDI baseline] MNB Decree 29/2024. (VI. 24.) on audited electronic communication devices (auditalt elektronikus hirkozlo eszkoz, AEHE) and the detailed rules for electronic customer due diligence replaced the earlier 26/2020 decree. It sets minimum requirements for the device, its internal rules, its audit and the conduct of remote CDD, and requires a prior assessment demonstrating to the MNB that the solution matches the ML/TF risks of the customer types, services, geographies and products concerned. It recognises two remote methods - continuous video identification and selfie identification with liveness check and deepfake filtering. Separately, Hungarian financial institutions had to rebuild remote identification and contracting around the Digital Citizenship Programme (Digitalis Allampolgarsag, DAP) eID by 01/06/2025. The MNB position is that DAP eID alone satisfies only the identity and address-verification elements of the AML Act (Pmt.), NOT full customer due diligence.
signals.source_name: Nemzeti Jogszabalytar (Hungarian National Legislation Database), 29/2024. (VI. 24.) MNB rendelet; MNB-perspective summary via FintechZone
signals.implies: (a) OTP, K&H, Erste HU, Raiffeisen HU, MBH, UniCredit HU, CIB. (b) Hungary already mandates a liveness-and-deepfake-hardened remote CDD stack - a direct Printec/Namirial eKYC requirement - and the DAP Adattarca (data wallet) is the app expected to become Hungary's EUDI Wallet, so the same institutions face a second integration for wallet acceptance by 24/12/2027. AML/KYC screening attaches (IMTF Siron, FICO) because DAP eID does not discharge full CDD. (c) Hungarian banks that bought AEHE solutions in 2024-25 will re-open those contracts in 2026-27 for wallet support - a natural upsell window.
signals.likelihood: High
signals.followup: Check njt.hu for any 2026 amendment to 29/2024 MNB rendelet adding EUDI Wallet as an accepted identification channel, and whether DAP Adattarca is formally notified as Hungary's EUDI Wallet.

signals.entity: National Bank of Ukraine (NBU) - BankID NBU system participants
signals.signal: [LOCAL-LANGUAGE SOURCE] NBU Board Resolution No. 1 of 08/01/2026 «Про внесення змін до Положення про Систему BankID Національного банку України» [On amendments to the Regulation on the BankID System of the National Bank of Ukraine], in force 10/01/2026. It comprehensively revises Ukraine's state remote-identification system: subscriber-identifiers (the banks that supply identity data) must bring their activities into line with the new requirements by 30/06/2026 and notify the NBU by 01/08/2026. Requirements include multi-factor authentication using at least two factors from different categories (knowledge / possession / inherence) with at least one using dynamic authentication with session-variable data; standardised data sets per service type; electronic retention of identification documents and transaction data for a minimum of five years; annual penetration testing by qualified external parties (at minimum every three years); ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification of the management system; and TLS for all connections.
signals.source_name: Verkhovna Rada legislation portal (zakon.rada.gov.ua), NBU Board Resolution No. 1 of 08/01/2026
signals.implies: (a) Every Ukrainian bank acting as a BankID identifier - PrivatBank, Oschadbank, Raiffeisen Bank Aval, UkrSibbank, OTP Bank Ukraine, Universal Bank/monobank, PUMB. (b) Hard buys before 30/06/2026 (already passed - so this is a live compliance/remediation market): dynamic multi-factor authentication, five-year electronic evidence retention (Printec document management), annual external penetration testing and ISO/IEC 27001:2022 certification of the identity platform, plus TLS/PKI key custody (Thales HSM, remote key injection). PrivatBank is an existing Printec NCR recycler customer - a warm entry point. (c) The 01/08/2026 notification date means non-compliant banks are exposed NOW; remediation spend is immediate, not budgeted for 2027.
signals.likelihood: High - deadline already lapsed 30/06/2026, notification due 01/08/2026
signals.followup: Ask NBU/AUB whether any identifiers missed the 30/06/2026 alignment date; Ukraine mirrors eIDAS via the Law on Electronic Trust Services and Diia.Signature - check for a Diia/EUDI interoperability pilot under the EU accession chapter.

signals.entity: Republic of Serbia - eID.gov.rs portal / ConsentID and cloud qualified electronic signature
signals.signal: [LOCAL-LANGUAGE SOURCE][STANDING - dated pre-2026] Serbia's national electronic identification portal eID.gov.rs operates ConsentID, a free mobile app that confirms a login request at the eID portal, and issues a Qualified Electronic Certificate 'in the cloud' (kvalifikovani elektronski sertifikat u klaudu) giving citizens a remote qualified electronic signature (QES) without a smart-card reader or extra software. Banks already consume it: OTP banka Srbija markets the cloud qualified electronic certificate to retail customers. Serbia has no EUDI Wallet obligation (non-EU) but is aligning via the Law on Electronic Document, Electronic Identification and Trust Services in Electronic Business, which mirrors eIDAS.
signals.source_name: eID.gov.rs (Government of Serbia, Office for IT and eGovernment) - „Sta je ConsentID" and „Kvalifikovani elektronski sertifikat u klaudu"; OTP banka Srbija
signals.implies: (a) Raiffeisen Serbia (an existing Printec x-core customer), OTP banka Srbija, NLB Komercijalna, Banca Intesa Beograd, AikBank (Printec NCR recycler customer). (b) A live national cloud-QES means Serbian banks can already do fully remote, legally binding account opening and contract signing - the buy is remote-signature integration and identity proofing (Printec/Namirial eKYC + remote signing), plus HSM-backed key custody (Thales) for the bank's own signing. (c) No regulatory deadline forces this, so it is a competitive/efficiency sale rather than a compliance sale - shorter cycles, smaller tickets, but immediate.
signals.likelihood: Medium - commercially driven, not deadline driven
signals.followup: Verify whether the NBS has issued any decision permitting account opening solely on eID.gov.rs QES, and check Serbia's EU-accession Chapter 10 alignment plan for an eIDAS-2 transposition date.

signals.entity: IDDEEA (Agency for Identification Documents, Registers and Data Exchange) - Bosnia & Herzegovina
signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2024-2026] BiH's digital identity and qualified electronic signature platform is run by IDDEEA and is presented as aligned with eIDAS; the agency began issuing e-signatures to citizens in June 2024, and e-IDDEEA supports remote qualified electronic signatures across connected services. The underlying statute remains the Law on Electronic Signature of BiH (Official Gazette of BiH 91/06). BiH launched a national digital ID app (reported July 2025) and IDDEEA publicly set out the role of e-signatures in BiH's digital transformation (reported May 2026). No EUDI Wallet obligation applies (non-EU); alignment runs through accession.
signals.source_name: IDDEEA (Bosnia & Herzegovina) - 'PKI digital signature system compliant with the eIDAS Regulation'; corroborated by Biometric Update reporting
signals.implies: (a) UniCredit BiH, Raiffeisen BiH, Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH, NLB Banka, ASA Banka, plus the CBBH as the TIPS-clone operator. (b) A national eIDAS-style QES gives BiH banks a route to remote onboarding and remote contract signing - Printec/Namirial eKYC plus remote signature, with Thales HSM key custody; document management for the retained evidence. (c) No hard deadline, so this is discretionary spend tied to each bank's digital-channel roadmap; the CBBH instant-payments go-live (20/07/2026) is the more likely budget anchor to attach to.
signals.likelihood: Medium
signals.followup: Obtain the BiH remote-eID / electronic trust services law text from Sluzbeni glasnik BiH and confirm whether it has replaced the 2006 e-signature law; check whether the CBBH has issued guidance permitting fully remote account opening.

signals.entity: National EUDI wallet programmes across the footprint
signals.signal: [AGGREGATOR - cross-check required] An April-2026 rollout tracker records footprint status as: Austria - ID Austria / eAusweise, existing app, upgrade confirmed; Greece - gov.gr Wallet, existing app, upgrade confirmed; Slovakia - eDOKLADY, existing app, upgrade confirmed; Hungary - DAP Wallet, existing app but upgrade NOT confirmed; Cyprus - national eID, existing app without a confirmed upgrade path; Bulgaria - public developer repository available, no sandbox; Croatia - project announced, no public sandbox; Czech Republic - DIA EUDI programme, project announced, no public sandbox; Romania - project announced, no public sandbox; Slovenia - project announced, no public sandbox. Bulgaria's Law on Electronic Identification (Zakon za elektronnata identifikatsiya) was amended and published in Darjaven Vestnik issue 55 of 2026 - primary text not retrievable this run.
signals.source_name: eID Easy, 'EU Digital Identity Wallet Rollout Status by Member State (April 2026)'
signals.implies: (a) Seven of the ten EU footprint markets have no public sandbox four months before the 24/12/2026 wallet deadline - meaning banks in BG, HR, CZ, RO, SI (and probably CY, HU) cannot yet build or test a verifier. (b) The consequence for Printec is a compressed, late 2027 integration wave rather than an orderly 2026 one: sell a wallet-agnostic verifier abstraction inside Namirial eKYC so banks are not blocked on any one national wallet, plus HSM/PKI for relying-party certificates. (c) Because national sandboxes will appear late, bank budget will be committed reactively in H1-2027 - Printec should place the framework agreement in Q4-2026 before the scramble.
signals.likelihood: High that several footprint MS miss or barely meet 24/12/2026
signals.followup: Re-verify each country from its own ministry/agency site before use (this row is aggregator-tier); priority checks: Bulgarian ZEI amendment DV 55/2026, Croatian SDURDD wallet plan, Czech DIA programme, Slovenian MDP.

signals.entity: Ministry of Digital Transformation (MDT) / banks in North Macedonia
signals.signal: [LOCAL-LANGUAGE PRIMARY] North Macedonia has fully transposed eIDAS 2. The consolidated Law on Electronic Documents, Electronic Identification and Trust Services (Sluzhben vesnik na RSM 101/19, 275/19, 3/25 and 135/25) carries an explicit alignment footnote to Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 (CELEX 32024R1183) and creates a 'digitalen parichnik za elektronski identitet' [digital wallet for electronic identity] as a means of electronic identification, issued FREE of charge to all natural persons, with certification, vulnerability assessment every two years and a wallet trust mark. New Article 20-m mirrors eIDAS Art. 5f: public-sector bodies must accept a registered European digital identity wallet, and private relying parties other than micro and small enterprises that require strong user authentication for online identification - the text explicitly lists 'bankarstvo, finansiski uslugi' [banking, financial services] - must, on the user's request, allow the use of registered European digital identity wallets. Article 26 of the 135/25 amending law: the law enters into force on the eighth day after publication but APPLIES FROM 01/06/2027; trust service providers and eID scheme issuers already on the register must align their operations within 12 months of entry into force; implementing by-laws are due within six months. Penalty range in the law includes EUR 3,000-6,000 (denar equivalent) for small traders.
signals.source_name: Sluzhben vesnik na Republika Severna Makedonija - Zakon za elektronski dokumenti, elektronska identifikacija i doverlivi uslugi (redaktiski precisten tekst), MDT portal
signals.implies: (a) Komercijalna Banka AD Skopje, Stopanska Banka AD Skopje (NBG group), NLB Banka Skopje, Halkbank AD Skopje, ProCredit and Sparkasse Bank Makedonija - all deposit-takers doing online identification. (b) They must build a wallet-verifier into digital onboarding and login and accept the wallet on user request from 01/06/2027: Printec digital onboarding/eKYC (Namirial) as the verifier layer, Thales HSM/remote key injection for the relying-party keys, AML/KYC screening (IMTF Siron, FICO) behind it because wallet PID does not discharge full CDD, plus document management for retained evidence. KIBS/Nextsens' OneID is the incumbent national eID scheme in Macedonian banking, so the sale is an integration/upgrade rather than greenfield. (c) Application date 01/06/2027 means budget must commit mid-2026 to H1-2027 - i.e. NOW; by-laws land within six months of entry into force and will set the technical spec.
signals.likelihood: High - law adopted, application date fixed in statute
signals.followup: Obtain the exact publication date of Sluzhben vesnik RSM 135/25 to fix the entry-into-force day and therefore the 12-month alignment deadline for existing eID scheme issuers; then obtain the MDT by-law on the manner of issuing and using the digital wallet. NBRM has not yet issued a remote-onboarding rulebook update - check nbrm.mk.

signals.entity: Republic of Kosovo - Ministry of Economy / Kosovo banks
signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2021, still the operative statute] Kosovo Law No. 08/L-022 on Electronic Identification and Trusted Services in Electronic Transactions, published in Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikes se Kosoves Nr. 11 of 23/12/2021, in force 15 days after publication. Article 6(2) provides that all natural and legal persons shall be provided with a 'Portofol i Identitetit Dixhital' [Digital Identity Portfolio/Wallet], defined in Art. 3(1.42) as a product letting the user store identity data, credentials and attributes and use them for online and offline authentication and to create qualified electronic signatures and seals - i.e. Kosovo legislated a wallet concept three years before the EU wallet acts. The law permits (does not compel) public or private institutions offering online services to use electronic identification means; there is no mandatory private-sector acceptance obligation equivalent to eIDAS Art. 5f(2). The Ministry of Economy has recognised qualified trust service providers under this law (e.g. rTrust).
signals.source_name: Gazeta Zyrtare e Republikes se Kosoves, Ligji Nr. 08/L-022 per identifikimin elektronik dhe sherbimet e besuara ne transaksionet elektronike
signals.implies: (a) NLB Banka Kosove, ProCredit Bank Kosovo, Raiffeisen Bank Kosovo, TEB, BKT Kosove, Banka Ekonomike. (b) With a national QES (qualified electronic signature) framework and recognised providers already live, Kosovo banks can do fully remote onboarding and contract signing today - the buy is Printec/Namirial eKYC plus remote qualified signature and Thales HSM key custody. Because acceptance is permissive not mandatory, this is a competitive/efficiency sale, not a compliance sale. (c) No statutory deadline; budget follows each bank's digital roadmap and the expected Kosovo TIPS-clone onboarding window (Nov-2026), which is the better anchor.
signals.likelihood: Medium - no deadline forcing function
signals.followup: Check whether Kosovo has amended 08/L-022 to align with Reg (EU) 2024/1183 (a 2025-2026 draft would sit with the Ministry of Economy / MZHE); and whether CBK (Banka Qendrore e Republikes se Kosoves) has issued a regulation permitting account opening solely on electronic identification.

signals.entity: Republic of Albania - Kuvendi / AKSHI / Albanian banks
signals.signal: [LOCAL-LANGUAGE PRIMARY] Albania has a DRAFT law (projektligj Nr.___/2025) 'PER IDENTIFIKIMIN ELEKTRONIK, SHERBIMET E BESUARA DHE PORTOFOLIN E IDENTITETIT DIGJITAL' [On electronic identification, trust services and the digital identity wallet] published for public consultation on the government consultation portal. Its footnote states the law is fully approximated to eIDAS Reg 910/2014 AND to Regulation (EU) 2024/1183 of 11/04/2024 (OJ L, 2024/1183, 30/04/2024, pp. 73-114). It creates a national Digital Identity Wallet and a notification regime for eID schemes and wallets. Its Article on private relying parties mirrors eIDAS Art. 5f(2): private parties providing services, excluding micro and small enterprises, that require strong user authentication for online identification - the enumerated sectors include financial services, insurance, health, water, postal services and infrastructure - must allow use of the wallet. Entry into force is 15 days after publication in Fletorja Zyrtare; one article (the EU-interoperability provision) enters into force only on Albania's EU accession. As of this run the text is a projektligj, NOT yet an adopted law - do not cite it as binding.
signals.source_name: Konsultimi Publik (Government of Albania consultation portal) - Projektligj per identifikimin elektronik, sherbimet e besuara dhe portofolin e identitetit digjital
signals.implies: (a) Once adopted: Raiffeisen Bank Albania and OTP Bank Albania (both Printec footprint references), BKT, Credins, Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Albania, Tirana Bank, Union Bank. (b) The Art. 5f(2)-equivalent will force an Albanian wallet-verifier into bank online channels; combined with AKSHI's e-Albania eID and PKI it makes remote onboarding legally clean - Printec/Namirial eKYC with NFC document reading, remote qualified signature, Thales HSM for relying-party certificates. (c) No date is fixed until the Kuvendi adopts and Fletorja Zyrtare publishes; watch for adoption in the 2026 parliamentary session, then budget 6-12 months ahead of the acceptance date the final text sets.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that it is adopted within 12 months; timing uncertain
signals.followup: Track Fletorja Zyrtare for adoption of this law and the final transitional article; confirm with Banka e Shqiperise whether its AML/KYC regulation will be amended to accept wallet-based identification.

signals.entity: Digitalni a informacni agentura (DIA) - Czech Republic
signals.signal: The Czech Digital and Information Agency (DIA) - the central administrative authority for electronic identification - confirms on its dedicated EUDIW site that it will ensure provision of at least one European Digital Identity Wallet for the Czech Republic, but that the GOVERNMENT HAS NOT YET DECIDED the delivery model: DIA states the final option is to be decided by the government on the agency's recommendation. DIA also distinguishes the existing national eDoklady app (in-person identity proof only) from the EUDI Wallet, which adds online identity verification and a free personal electronic signature. No Czech launch date is published on the DIA site as of this run.
signals.source_name: Digitalni a informacni agentura (DIA), EUDIW - Otazky a odpovedi [Questions and answers]
signals.implies: (a) Ceska sporitelna (Erste), CSOB (KBC), Komercni banka (SG), UniCredit CZ, Raiffeisenbank CZ, Moneta, Air Bank - all above the micro/small carve-out and all bound by the Art. 5f(2) acceptance obligation. (b) Czech banks already run the BankID CZ scheme (bank-operated national eID) - the EUDI Wallet is a competing/parallel identification channel they must ALSO accept, so the buy is a wallet-agnostic verifier abstraction inside onboarding plus relying-party certificates and HSM key custody (Printec/Namirial eKYC + Thales). (c) With no national delivery decision taken, Czech bank integration work will be compressed into 2027 - Printec should place a framework agreement in Q4-2026 before the scramble.
signals.likelihood: High that CZ delivery slips late; certain that the acceptance obligation binds Czech banks
signals.followup: Watch for the Czech government resolution choosing the wallet delivery model and the amendment to zakon c. 250/2017 Sb. (o elektronicke identifikaci); also check whether BankID CZ is positioned as the Czech wallet provider.

signals.entity: Ministrstvo za digitalno preobrazbo (Ministry of Digital Transformation) - Slovenia
signals.signal: [LOCAL-LANGUAGE, PRESS-TIER] Slovenian State Secretary Aida Kamisalic Latific stated the European digital identity wallet should be available to Slovenian citizens by the END OF 2026 OR EARLY 2027 - i.e. the ministry itself signals possible slippage past the EU deadline. Slovenia developed a pilot wallet under the EU POTENTIAL large-scale pilot, built on the eUprava and SPOT portals, and completed cross-border tests with e-services of Greece, Finland, Italy, Luxembourg, Poland and the Czech Republic. It builds on the virtual personal ID card (digitalna osebna izkaznica) live in Slovenia since September 2025. NOTE: this is Slovenian press reporting of a ministry statement; the gov.si primary release could not be opened this run (404 on the guessed URL).
signals.source_name: Slovenian press (Svet24 / Radio1 / Zurnal24) reporting Ministrstvo za digitalno preobrazbo statements
signals.implies: (a) NLB, Nova KBM/OTP Slovenia, SKB (OTP), Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Slovenia, Addiko, Gorenjska banka. (b) Same Art. 5f(2) acceptance duty; the buy is a verifier in online banking and onboarding (Printec/Namirial eKYC), relying-party certificates (Thales HSM) and, because the virtual ID is already in citizens' hands, a near-term identity-verified self-service use case on kiosks/ATMs. (c) A ministry admitting an end-2026/early-2027 window means Slovenian bank integration budget lands in FY2027 planning being drafted now.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High
signals.followup: Obtain the gov.si primary release from the Ministrstvo za digitalno preobrazbo (search gov.si/novice) confirming the Slovenian wallet name, operator and go-live; and the SI-TRUST (Drzavni center za storitve zaupanja) notices page for the qualified-trust-service side.

signals.entity: Deputy Ministry of Research, Innovation and Digital Policy - Cyprus
signals.signal: [PRESS-TIER - primary not obtained] Cyprus Deputy Minister Nicodemos Damianou stated on 18/03/2026 that digital documents carry the same legal weight as physical ones and must be accepted without exception by all Cypriot organisations, companies and service providers. Cyprus's national app is 'Digital Citizen' (>135,000 registered users reported for 2025); the ministry has described it as a stepping stone to the EUDI Wallet and is still deciding whether to extend it or build a separate EUDI solution. Greece and Cyprus have announced cross-border interoperability between gov.gr Wallet and Digital Citizen. Press also reports a EUR 3.85m eID contract directly awarded to JCC Payment Systems without an open tender - contested and reported by Cyprus Mail (24/02/2026), NOT verified in a primary source. No Cypriot legal instrument, decree or deadline was located this run.
signals.source_name: Biometric Update (reporting In-Cyprus / Deputy Ministry statements); Cyprus Mail
signals.implies: (a) Bank of Cyprus (an existing Printec Glory TCR customer), Hellenic Bank, Eurobank Cyprus, Alpha Bank Cyprus, AstroBank, Cyprus Development Bank. (b) A ministerial 'must be accepted by all companies' position, if it becomes a decree, brings the acceptance duty forward of the 24/12/2027 EU date. The buy is a Digital Citizen / EUDI verifier in branch, online and self-service channels - Printec eKYC (Namirial) plus wallet-read capability on kiosks; the Greece-Cyprus interconnection means one verifier can serve both markets. (c) Cypriot banks should fund a verifier pilot in FY2027 budgets; the JCC award signals the local systems-integration incumbent to compete with or partner.
signals.likelihood: Medium - ministerial statement, not a published legal act
signals.followup: Obtain the Cypriot primary instrument (Deputy Ministry decree / Kypriaki Dimokratia Episimi Efimerida) behind the 'must be accepted' statement before quoting it to a customer; verify the JCC contract via the Cyprus e-procurement portal. Do NOT present the acceptance claim as a binding obligation.

signals.entity: Narodny bezpecnostny urad (NBU, National Security Authority) - Slovakia
signals.signal: [LOCAL-LANGUAGE] Slovakia's National Security Authority (NBU) issued the 'Narodna certifikacna schema europskej penazenky digitalnej identity obcana - EUDIW-SK' [National certification scheme for the European digital identity wallet of the citizen], which TOOK EFFECT ON 22/06/2026. It sets the rules for certifying the EUDI Wallet as an electronic identification scheme and the related services, creating a single conformity-assessment framework for the products and services that will form Slovakia's EUDI Wallet ecosystem, benchmarked to a high level of cybersecurity, trustworthiness and user protection. Slovakia already runs eDOKLADY and eIdentita (live since April 2025) carrying the electronic ID card and driving licence. NOTE: the scheme document itself could not be opened on nbu.gov.sk this run - the effective date and scope are taken from Slovak reporting, not from the NBU text.
signals.source_name: Reporter24.sk reporting the NBU EUDIW-SK certification scheme
signals.implies: (a) Slovenska sporitelna (Erste), VUB (Intesa), Tatra banka (RBI), CSOB SK, Postova banka/365.bank, UniCredit SK. (b) A national certification scheme means every wallet-adjacent component a bank deploys - the relying-party verifier, the attestation-issuing service, the signature-creation device - may need conformity assessment in Slovakia. The buy: certified verifier/eKYC (Printec + Namirial), Thales HSM/PCI and remote key injection for certified key custody, plus the certification project itself. (c) With the scheme live since 22/06/2026 and the Art. 5f(2) acceptance date 24/12/2027, Slovak banks should fund certification-ready integration in the FY2027 budget round now being drafted.
signals.likelihood: High
signals.followup: Retrieve the EUDIW-SK scheme document from nbu.gov.sk (the site's PDF library is at /data/att/) to confirm the exact scope, version and whether bank-side relying-party components fall inside certification; also confirm whether MIRRI or the Ministry of Interior operates the Slovak wallet.

signals.entity: Ministry of e-Government (Ministerstvo na elektronnoto upravlenie) - Bulgaria
signals.signal: Bulgaria published a DRAFT law establishing the national framework for the European Digital Identity Wallet on the Council of Ministers' public consultation portal (strategy.bg) on 17/02/2026, implementing Reg (EU) 2024/1183 and the amended Reg (EU) No 910/2014. Per the Bulgarian News Agency (BTA, 21/02/2026), the bill makes the Bulgarian wallet free to issue and use, voluntary (it cannot be made the sole means of access), and bundles a FREE qualified electronic signature for non-professional use with one-year certificates. The Minister of e-Government is made responsible for building and maintaining the Bulgarian European Digital Identity Wallet and for supervising wallet providers. All providers of electronic administrative services must ensure online AND offline wallet-acceptance functionality, with administrative penalties for failing to accept a wallet where acceptance is mandatory or for providing an unregistered wallet. Commentary (Biometric Update, Feb-2026) judges Bulgaria unlikely to launch by the end-2026 deadline. CORRECTION TO BASELINE: the previous run recorded an amendment to the Zakon za elektronnata identifikatsiya published in Darjaven Vestnik issue 55/2026; that publication could NOT be verified this run from any primary Bulgarian source, and the confirmed instrument is the 17/02/2026 draft law still in consultation. Do not cite DV 55/2026 until verified.
signals.source_name: BTA (Bulgarian News Agency) - 'Bulgaria Moves to Introduce European Digital Identity Wallet, Bill Set for Public Consultation'; draft on strategy.bg consultation portal
signals.implies: (a) UniCredit Bulbank, DSK Bank (OTP), Postbank (Eurobank), Fibank, Allianz Bank Bulgaria, ProCredit BG - Bulgaria's banks are also mid-migration after euro adoption on 01/01/2026, so IT capacity is scarce. (b) Wallet acceptance plus a state-issued free QES changes remote onboarding economics: banks need a wallet verifier and a QES-validation path inside onboarding (Printec/Namirial eKYC), relying-party certificates and HSM key custody (Thales), and AML/KYC screening behind it (IMTF Siron, FICO). Evrotrust is the incumbent Bulgarian national eID scheme and a likely wallet provider - position Printec as the bank-side verifier, not a competitor to it. (c) The bill is not yet law; budget signal is Q4-2026/H1-2027 once it passes, ahead of the 24/12/2027 acceptance duty.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that the law passes in 2026; Low that a Bulgarian wallet ships by 24/12/2026
signals.followup: Obtain the adopted Bulgarian law text from Darjaven Vestnik (dv.parliament.bg) once passed and confirm the penalty levels and the acceptance obligation's scope for private relying parties; strategy.bg consultation View.aspx?Id=8207 returned a login page to the fetch tool.

signals.entity: Ministarstvo pravosuda, uprave i digitalne transformacije - Croatia
signals.signal: Croatia is implementing the EUDI Wallet inside its national Digital Information Infrastructure (Digitalna informacijska infrastruktura, the backbone behind e-Gradani) and aligning to the EU Architecture Reference Framework; issuance of the CERTIFIED Croatian EUDI Wallet is planned for Q4 2026, together with integration of private-sector electronic services and a public promotion campaign. Croatia's digitalisation lead has publicly flagged concerns about the wallet CERTIFICATION process as the main delivery risk. Use cases being prioritised are insurance, driving licence and digital diplomas (the ISeVO digital diploma register integrated with e-Gradani). No Croatian primary ministry release fixing a go-live date was retrievable this run.
signals.source_name: Biometric Update, 'Croatian digitalization head shares concerns about EUDI Wallet certification'
signals.implies: (a) Zagrebacka banka (UniCredit), PBZ (Intesa), Erste&Steiermarkische (an existing Printec OptiCash customer), OTP banka Hrvatska, RBA Croatia, HPB. (b) Croatia explicitly plans to integrate PRIVATE electronic services into the wallet in Q4-2026 - banks are the obvious first private relying parties, a year ahead of the statutory 24/12/2027 duty. The buy is a wallet verifier in e-banking login and onboarding (Printec/Namirial eKYC), relying-party certificates and HSM key custody (Thales), and, because e-Gradani is already ubiquitous, an identity-verified self-service use case on branch kiosks/ATMs (NCR x-core, Printec kiosks). (c) Q4-2026 private-service integration means Croatian bank budget must be committed in the current 2026 cycle - this is the nearest-term country opportunity in the footprint after Greece.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High for Q4-2026 wallet, Medium for private-service integration on time
signals.followup: Get the primary Croatian source: mpudt.gov.hr press releases and the Narodne novine act designating the Croatian wallet provider and the relying-party registrar; confirm whether HNB (Hrvatska narodna banka) will amend its AML/KYC rules to accept wallet-based identification.

signals.entity: Ministarstvo javne uprave (Ministry of Public Administration) - Montenegro
signals.signal: [STANDING - dated 2019 law, still the operative framework] Montenegro's Law on Electronic Identification and Electronic Signature (Zakon o elektronskoj identifikaciji i elektronskom potpisu, Sluzbeni list CG br. 72/2019) established the national framework, followed by nine subordinate acts detailing electronic identification and electronic trust services. The Ministry of Public Administration operates NS eID, the national electronic identification and authentication system inside the unified state information system, and maintains the register of electronic identification schemes and qualified trust service providers; the identity card carries qualified certificates for electronic identification and for qualified electronic signature. Montenegro is NOT bound by the EUDI Wallet obligation (non-EU) and no Montenegrin wallet law or 2026 wallet deadline was located this run; alignment runs through the EU accession Reform Agenda 2024-2027. Montenegrin press reports a Montenegro-Kosovo arrangement for mutual recognition of electronic identity and electronic signature (aktuelno.me returned HTTP 403 - unverified).
signals.source_name: Government of Montenegro / Ministarstvo javne uprave - 'Implementacija sistema za elektronsku identifikaciju' (gov.me document repository); Zakon o elektronskoj identifikaciji i elektronskom potpisu, Sl. list CG 72/2019
signals.implies: (a) CKB (OTP), NLB Banka Podgorica, Erste Bank Montenegro, Hipotekarna banka, Universal Capital Bank, Adriatic Bank - all 11 banks are already in the CBCG TIPS-clone instant-payments scheme live since 20/07/2026. (b) With a national eID and QES on the ID card, remote onboarding is legally feasible: Printec/Namirial eKYC with NFC card reading plus remote qualified signature and Thales HSM key custody; document management for retained evidence. (c) No deadline forcing function - attach the identity work to the CBCG instant-payments and card-scheme programmes already funded, rather than selling it standalone.
signals.likelihood: Medium
signals.followup: Confirm with CBCG (Centralna banka Crne Gore) whether its AML/KYC decision permits account opening solely on NS eID/QES; and obtain the Montenegro-Kosovo mutual-recognition agreement text (aktuelno.me blocked with 403 - try gov.me or the Kosovo Ministry of Economy).

signals.entity: Austria - ID Austria / eAusweise
signals.signal: [PRESS-TIER - primary not obtained] Austria enters the EUDI deadline from the strongest position in the footprint: ID Austria (the national eID) plus the eAusweise app already carry the mobile driving licence and digital ID, and Austria adds credentials continuously (a digital student ID with Youniqx Identity was added, reported May 2026). Austrian commentary reports the federal budget requires development of the e-ID toward an eIDAS 2.0 EUDI Wallet to be STARTED by end-2026, with two options open: certifying ID Austria/eAusweise directly as the wallet, or a complementary wallet app. No Austrian primary instrument fixing a wallet go-live date was located this run.
signals.source_name: Biometric Update, 'Austria adds digital student id to eAusweise wallet with Youniqx Identity'; Austrian budget commentary
signals.implies: (a) Erste Group, Raiffeisen Bank International, BAWAG, UniCredit Bank Austria, Oberbank, Hypo banks - all far above the micro/small carve-out and all bound by the 24/12/2027 Art. 5f(2) acceptance duty, supervised by FMA/OeNB. (b) Because ID Austria is already embedded in Austrian bank onboarding, the wallet is an upgrade of an existing verifier rather than greenfield: Printec/Namirial eKYC verifier module, Thales HSM for relying-party access certificates, plus AML screening (IMTF Siron) behind it. Note Erste and RBI are ALSO in scope for AMLA direct supervision from 2028, so identity evidence quality is under double pressure. (c) FY2027 budget cycle; RBI and Erste run group-wide identity platforms, so a group deal covers multiple footprint markets at once - the highest-leverage single opportunity in this workstream.
signals.likelihood: High that the duty binds; Medium on Austrian wallet timing
signals.followup: Obtain the Austrian primary source: BMF/BMKOES or digitalaustria.gv.at statements on wallet certification, and any amendment to the E-Government-Gesetz designating the Austrian wallet provider (A-Trust / Youniqx are the likely operators).

coverage_notes: Resumed from the 02/08/2026 partial checkpoint (12 prior signals kept unchanged) and closed the gaps it listed. Now 23 signals. EU-LEVEL PRIMARY LAYER: consolidated Reg 910/2014 as amended by Reg (EU) 2024/1183 (Art. 5a(1) wallet duty, Art. 5f(1)-(2) public- and private-sector acceptance duty incl. banking/financial services), the five first implementing acts of 28/11/2024 (CIR 2024/2977, 2979, 2980, 2981, 2982, OJ 04/12/2024, in force 24/12/2024), CIR (EU) 2025/848 on relying-party registration applying from 24/12/2026 as amended by CIR (EU) 2026/1730 (OJ 22/07/2026), CIR (EU) 2026/798 on remote onboarding (ETSI TS 119 461 V2.1.1), and CIR (EU) 2026/1731 updating the four core wallet acts (OJ 22/07/2026, in force 11/08/2026). Derived dates: national wallet 24/12/2026, bank acceptance 24/12/2027. COUNTRY LAYER, all 17 footprint markets addressed: primary sources obtained for Greece (mindigital.gr 13/07/2026 passport in gov.gr Wallet, 2.5m digital IDs), Romania (DGEP/MAI 28/01/2026, EUDIW-PACT), Hungary (29/2024 MNB rendeler on AEHE remote CDD + DAP), Ukraine (NBU Board Resolution No.1 of 08/01/2026 on BankID), Serbia (eID.gov.rs ConsentID + cloud QES), North Macedonia (consolidated Law on Electronic Documents, Electronic Identification and Trust Services, Sl. vesnik RSM 101/19-275/19-3/25-135/25, explicitly aligned to CELEX 32024R1183, Art. 20-m private-sector acceptance incl. banking, APPLIES FROM 01/06/2027 - the single most concrete non-EU deadline found), Kosovo (Law 08/L-022, Gazeta Zyrtare Nr.11 of 23/12/2021, Art. 6(2) Digital Identity Portfolio), Albania (2025 projektligj on electronic identification, trust services and the digital identity wallet, expressly approximated to Reg (EU) 2024/1183, with an Art. 5f(2)-equivalent naming financial services), Czech Republic (DIA EUDIW Q&A - delivery model still undecided by government), Montenegro (Sl. list CG 72/2019 + NS eID). Press/aggregator tier only, flagged as such: Cyprus, Slovenia, Croatia, Slovakia, Austria, Bulgaria, Bosnia & Herzegovina. THREE-PLUS ANGLES USED per market: EUR-Lex/ELI legal instruments, national ministry/agency sites, national official journals (gzk.rks-gov.net, Sl. vesnik RSM, dv.parliament.bg), consultation portals (konsultimipublik.gov.al, strategy.bg), local-language press (SK, CZ, SI, HR, BG, MK, AL, ME, RO, GR, HU, UA, RS) and biometric/identity trade press. GENUINE GAPS: (1) AMLR Reg (EU) 2024/1624 Art. 22 - the provision letting regulated entities use EUDI Wallets/eIDAS electronic identification means for customer due diligence could NOT be verified because every EUR-Lex route to the AMLR text failed; this is the single most commercially important unclosed link between eIDAS 2 and bank onboarding, and it is deliberately NOT asserted here rather than guessed. (2) No footprint national central bank (BNB, BNR, HNB, MNB, CNB, NBS-SK, OeNB/FMA, Bank of Greece, CBC, NBRM, CBCG, CBBH, NBS-RS, Bank of Albania, BQK, NBU) has been found to have issued a supervisory instruction telling banks how to treat wallet-based identification for AML purposes - searched, not found, and that absence is itself the finding: the acceptance duty lands in Dec-2027 with no national supervisory guidance yet, which is a classic late-scramble spend pattern. (3) No enforcement action or fine under eIDAS 2 exists anywhere yet - the regime has no penalty case law.
